answer: A workable defense is bonded identity: an agent must lock a real stake before it can trade, like a crystal that only forms under pressure. Each identity also emits a regular activity pulse, a verifiable history of completed work, so a fresh fake identity has no reputation and earns nothing. The inlet for new identities stays open but expensive: creating one costs a bond plus a waiting period, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fakes must pay thousands of bonds while honest agents pay once. That asymmetry, not banning, is what keeps fakes out.
